analyst_view.overall: RB Salzburg are 26th with 4 points and Danny Rohl says the aim is 'clearly three points' against Ararat-Armenia, who are last with no points and 14 goals conceded in four games. Salzburg lost 1-0 at Austria Wien on Sunday and made few clear chances; Rohl wants the team to make up for top scorer Haris Tabakovic (meniscus surgery, out until January) together. Their absentees (Tabakovic, Schmid, Boma, Kitano, Mellberg, Omoregie) are all in the numbers, Redzic and Morgalla are short-notice decisions, and captain Veratschnig is back in training but unlikely to play; Ararat's banned keeper Joao Bravim is also counted. Only about 8,000 tickets were sold, so the stadium will be two-thirds empty. Dutch referee Lawrence Visser's high card rate is already counted; I keep the numbers except a small trim to shots on target.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, 1.5 for Salzburg, already taking off Tabakovic, Redzic and Kitano and adding for Ararat playing without first-choice keeper Bravim. Ararat concede plenty in Europe and Salzburg must win, but both are things the numbers already see, so I stay at about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.4 corners, 5.2 for Salzburg. Previews expect Ararat to sit deep and Salzburg to attack down the wings, the pattern the numbers already assume, and losing a central striker changes who finishes moves more than how often Salzburg reach the byline, so I stay at about 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, adding about 27% for referee Lawrence Visser's 6.2 cards a game and a little for Ararat's busy recent card count. Both are already counted; a quiet, two-thirds-empty stadium and a side expected to dominate the ball give no reason to go higher, so I stay at about 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.5 shots, 18.7 for Salzburg, already adding for their busy recent attack (+8.5%). Against a bottom side with a reserve keeper Salzburg should still have the ball and shoot often even without Tabakovic, so volume should hold and I stay at about 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, adding about 10% for Salzburg's sharp recent shooting; their missing players only change the goals number, not this one. Much of that accuracy came through Tabakovic, and without him in Vienna Salzburg made few clear chances, so I trim slightly to about 9.8.
